concerns.text: Task T015 (validate_schema.py) is marked [P] (parallel-safe) but has an explicit dependency on T014 (generation). Validation cannot run in parallel with generation; it must be sequential. This violates the 'Producer before consumer' rule and the [P] tag correctness.

Task T016 (hash_artifacts.py) is marked [P] but depends on T015 (validation) and T014 (generation). Hashing the artifact requires the artifact to exist and be validated first. Marking this as parallel-safe is a semantic ordering violation.
Task T023 (hash_artifacts.py) is marked [P] but depends on T021/T021b (analysis results). Hashing the results JSON requires the results to be generated first. The [P] tag is incorrect here.
Task T030 (hash_artifacts.py) is marked [P] but depends on T028 (t-test results). Hashing requires the results to exist. The [P] tag is incorrect.
Task T033 (hash_artifacts.py) is marked [P] but depends on T032 (report generation). Hashing the report requires the report to exist. The [P] tag is incorrect.

Task T014b (measure metrics) is marked as dependent on T014, but T014 is the generation task. While the dependency is noted, the task description implies it runs 'immediately after' T014. If T014 is a long-running script, T014b should be a post-processing step or part of T014's exit logic, not a separate parallel task. The current separation risks race conditions if T014b is attempted before T014 fully writes the file.

Task T021c (measure metrics) is marked dependent on T021. Similar to T014b, if T021 is a long-running script, T021c must be strictly sequential. The [P] tag is not present here, but the dependency logic needs to ensure T021c does not run before T021 completes.

Task T030 is marked [P] but explicitly states 'Dependency: Must run after T028'. This is a direct contradiction. A task cannot be parallel-safe if it has a hard sequential dependency on a preceding task in the same phase.
